senses.def: something you want to achieve and are working toward
examples: My goal is to run a marathon before I turn forty.
The company set an ambitious goal of cutting emissions in half.

senses.def: a point scored by getting the ball into the net, or the net and frame itself
examples: She scored the winning goal in the final minute.
The ball hit the post and bounced away from the goal.

senses.def: (usually God) the being that many religions believe created and rules the universe
examples: Many people pray to God for strength in hard times.
Do you believe in God?

senses.def: one of many spirits that some religions worship as having power over nature or people
examples: Zeus was the king of the Greek gods.
The ancient Egyptians had a god of the sun.

note: Capitalize God for the one god of a religion. "Oh my God" is common but some people find it offensive; "oh my gosh" is softer.

senses.def: a valuable yellow metal used for jewelry, coins, and as an investment
examples: The ring is made of solid gold.
Investors often buy gold when the stock market is falling.

senses.def: a gold medal, given to the winner of a competition
examples: She won gold in the 100-meter sprint.

senses.def: made of gold, or having its bright yellow color
examples: He wore a gold watch to the wedding.
The invitation was printed in gold letters.

note: "Gold" is used for things made of the metal or its color; "golden" is more poetic or figurative (a golden opportunity).

senses.def: made of gold, or bright yellow like gold
examples: The king wore a golden crown.
The field was full of golden wheat.

senses.def: very good, special, or likely to bring success
examples: This is a golden opportunity to expand into new markets.
The 1960s were the golden age of television.

senses.def: a game in which players hit a small ball into a series of holes using clubs, in as few shots as possible
examples: My father plays golf every Saturday morning.
They discussed the deal over a round of golf.

senses.def: of high quality, pleasant, or at an acceptable standard
examples: This is a really good restaurant.
We had good weather for the whole trip.

senses.def: able to do something well
examples: She's very good at math.
He is good with children.

senses.def: helpful or healthy for someone, or morally right and kind
examples: Fresh vegetables are good for you.
It was good of you to help us move.

senses.def: behavior that is morally right, or something that benefits someone
examples: The battle between good and evil is an old theme in stories.
Complaining won't do any good.

note: Irregular: good – better – best. Use "well" as the adverb (She sings well). "For good" means "forever".

senses.def: what you say when you or another person is leaving
examples: Goodbye, everyone. See you on Monday!

senses.def: the act of saying goodbye when someone leaves
examples: We said our goodbyes at the airport.
It was a tearful goodbye after twenty years together.

note: "Wave/kiss goodbye to something" can also mean you will lose it: You can kiss your deposit goodbye.

senses.def: the quality of being kind, honest, and morally good
examples: She believes in the basic goodness of people.

senses.def: used to express surprise, often in phrases like "my goodness"
examples: My goodness, look how tall you've grown!
Thank goodness you're safe.

senses.def: things that are made to be sold, or things that someone owns and can move
examples: The store sells sporting goods and outdoor gear.
Tariffs raised the price of imported goods.

note: Always plural; there is no "a good" in this sense. Use "a product" or "an item" for one.

senses.def: very beautiful or attractive, or very pleasant
examples: You look gorgeous in that dress.
We had gorgeous weather for the beach party.

note: Informal and enthusiastic. Common for people, places, food, and weather.

senses.def: to officially control a country, state, or its people and make its laws
examples: The country was governed by the military for ten years.
The party has governed the state since 2010.

senses.def: to control or strongly influence how something happens or is done
examples: Strict rules govern the use of personal data.
Her decisions are governed by fear rather than logic.

senses.def: the way a country, company, or organization is controlled and how decisions are made
examples: Investors are demanding better corporate governance.
The report criticized the poor governance of the city's schools.

note: Formal; common in business, politics, and academic writing.

senses.def: the group of people who officially control a country or state
examples: The government announced new measures to reduce inflation.
Many people don't trust the government to protect their privacy.

senses.def: the system or activity of governing a country
examples: She studied government and economics in college.
The country moved toward democratic government.

note: In American English "the administration" often means the president's government. Pronounced /ˈɡʌvərmənt/ in fast speech.

senses.def: the elected head of a US state, or the official head of a region or colony
examples: The governor declared a state of emergency after the floods.
She is running for governor of Texas.

senses.def: a person who leads or is on the board of an institution such as a central bank
examples: The central bank governor warned that rates could rise again.

senses.def: to take hold of something suddenly and roughly
examples: He grabbed my arm to stop me from falling.
The thief grabbed her bag and ran.

senses.def: to quickly get or take something, often because you are busy
examples: Let's grab a coffee before the meeting.
I'll grab a seat near the front.

senses.def: to get someone's attention or interest
examples: The headline was designed to grab readers' attention.

note: "Up for grabs" means available for anyone to try to get: The top job is up for grabs.

senses.def: a smooth, attractive way of moving, or a calm and polite way of behaving
examples: The dancer moved across the stage with grace.
She accepted defeat with grace and congratulated her rival.

senses.def: extra time allowed before something must be done or paid
examples: The bank gave us a ten-day grace period to pay the bill.

senses.def: in Christianity, God's kindness and love toward people
examples: They believe they were saved by the grace of God.

note: "Saving grace" = the one good thing about something bad. "Say grace" = pray before a meal.

senses.def: a letter or number given to show the quality of a student's work
examples: She got good grades in all her science classes.
What grade did you get on the history test?

senses.def: one of the school years in the US, from first to twelfth
examples: My son is in third grade this year.

senses.def: a level of quality, size, or rank
examples: The factory uses only high-grade steel.

senses.def: to give a mark to a student's work, or to sort things by quality
examples: The teacher spent the weekend grading essays.
Eggs are graded by size.

note: American: "grade" for both school marks and school year (British: "mark" and "year"). Turkish "sınıf" = grade, not "class".

senses.def: slowly and in small steps over a period of time
examples: The patient's condition gradually improved over the next few weeks.
Add the flour gradually, stirring all the time.

note: Opposite: suddenly, abruptly.

senses.def: a person who has completed a university degree, or (in the US) high school
examples: She is a graduate of Stanford Law School.
Many recent college graduates struggle to find jobs.

senses.def: to complete your studies and receive a degree or diploma
examples: He graduated from high school in 2019.
She graduated with honors in chemistry.

senses.def: relating to studies done after a first university degree
examples: He's applying to graduate school next fall.

note: Noun /ˈɡrædʒuət/, verb /ˈɡrædʒueɪt/. Say "graduate from a school", not "graduate a school" (a common Turkish-speaker error).

senses.def: the seeds of plants like wheat and rice used as food, or one such seed
examples: The country exports large amounts of grain.
Choose whole grain bread for more fiber.

senses.def: a very small piece of something like sand or salt, or a small amount of a quality
examples: There's a grain of sand in my shoe.
There's a grain of truth in what he said.

senses.def: the natural pattern of lines in wood or fabric
examples: Sand the wood in the direction of the grain.

note: "Take something with a grain of salt" (US) = don't completely believe it. "Go against the grain" = be unusual or unnatural for you.

senses.def: impressive in size, appearance, or importance
examples: The hotel has a grand staircase in the lobby.
They have grand plans to rebuild the city center.

senses.def: including everything; final
examples: The grand total came to over two thousand dollars.

senses.def: (informal) a thousand dollars
examples: He paid ten grand for that used car.

note: "Grand" meaning $1,000 never takes -s: "five grand".

senses.def: the father of your mother or father
examples: My grandfather taught me how to fish when I was six.
Her grandfather emigrated from Italy in the 1950s.

note: Informal: grandpa. To specify the side of the family, say maternal (mother's) or paternal (father's) grandfather.

senses.def: the mother of your mother or father
examples: My grandmother makes the best apple pie.
She was raised by her grandmother after her parents died.

note: Babaanne = paternal grandmother; anneanne = maternal grandmother. English uses one word for both.

senses.tr: büyükanne veya büyükbaba; (çoğul) büyükanne ve büyükbaba
senses.def: a parent of your father or mother
examples: We spend every Thanksgiving with my grandparents.
Many grandparents help take care of their grandchildren.

senses.def: money given by a government or organization for a particular purpose, such as research
examples: The lab received a federal grant to study climate change.
She applied for a grant to fund her documentary.

senses.def: to officially give or allow someone something they have asked for
examples: The judge granted him permission to leave the country.
She was granted asylum in Canada.

senses.def: to admit that something is true, especially before arguing a different point
examples: I grant that the plan is expensive, but it will save money long term.

note: "Take something/someone for granted" = not appreciate it because you expect it to always be there.

senses.def: related to drawings, images, and design, especially in printing or on screens
examples: She works as a graphic designer for an ad agency.
The novel was adapted into a graphic novel.

senses.def: showing or describing something unpleasant, especially violence or sex, in very clear detail
examples: The movie contains graphic violence.
He gave a graphic description of the accident.

senses.def: a picture, chart, or design, especially one on a computer screen
examples: The article includes a graphic showing the rise in prices.

senses.def: pictures, designs, and images, especially those made by computer
examples: The new video game has amazing graphics.
You'll need a powerful graphics card to run this software.

senses.def: to take and hold something firmly
examples: She grasped the rope with both hands.
He grasped my hand and shook it warmly.

senses.def: to understand something, especially something difficult
examples: It took me a while to grasp the main idea of the theory.
They failed to grasp how serious the situation was.

senses.def: understanding of a subject, or a firm hold on something
examples: She has a good grasp of French grammar.
Success is finally within our grasp.

senses.def: a common plant with thin green leaves that covers fields, parks, and lawns
examples: The kids were lying on the grass in the park.
Please keep off the grass.

note: "The grass is always greener on the other side" = other people's situations always seem better (Komşunun tavuğu komşuya kaz görünür).

senses.def: feeling or showing thanks because someone has helped you or been kind
examples: I'm really grateful for all your help with the move.
We'd be grateful if you could reply by Friday.

note: Grateful TO a person FOR a thing. "I would be grateful if…" is a polite formal request in emails.

senses.def: a place in the ground where a dead person is buried
examples: They put flowers on their mother's grave every spring.
He took the secret to his grave.

senses.def: very serious and worrying
examples: Officials expressed grave concern about the safety of the dam.
This is a grave mistake that could cost lives.

note: The adjective is formal. "Turn in his grave" = a dead person would be very upset about something happening now.

senses.def: the natural force that pulls objects toward each other and makes things fall to the ground
examples: The moon's gravity causes the ocean tides.
Astronauts train to work without gravity.

senses.def: how serious or important a situation is
examples: He didn't seem to understand the gravity of the situation.

senses.def: having the color of smoke or clouds on a rainy day; (of hair) turning white with age
examples: It was a cold, gray morning in November.
My dad's hair started going gray in his forties.

senses.def: the color between black and white
examples: The walls are painted a soft gray.

note: American spelling: gray; British: grey. "A gray area" = something unclear, not clearly right or wrong.

senses.def: very good, enjoyable, or useful
examples: We had a great time at the concert.
That's a great idea!

senses.def: very large in amount, size, or degree
examples: The new law will be of great importance to small businesses.
She lived to a great age.

senses.def: very important, famous, or talented
examples: He's one of the greatest writers of his generation.

senses.def: very much; to a large degree
examples: Your help is greatly appreciated.
Prices vary greatly from one region to another.

note: Formal. Usually used with verbs and past participles, not adjectives: say "very happy", not "greatly happy".

senses.def: having the color of grass and leaves
examples: She has bright green eyes.
The hills turn green after the spring rains.

senses.def: relating to protecting the environment
examples: The city is investing in green energy like wind and solar.
More companies are trying to go green.

senses.def: the color of grass, or an area of grass in a town or on a golf course
examples: The room was decorated in green and white.

note: "Give the green light" = give permission. "Green" can also mean inexperienced: He's still green.

senses.def: a glass building used for growing plants that need warmth and protection
examples: My aunt grows tomatoes in a small greenhouse behind the house.

senses.def: relating to gases that trap heat in the earth's atmosphere
examples: Cars and power plants produce large amounts of greenhouse gases.
The greenhouse effect is warming the planet.

senses.def: to say hello to someone or welcome them when they arrive
examples: The host greeted each guest at the door.
She greeted me with a warm hug.

senses.def: to react to something in a particular way
examples: The announcement was greeted with loud applause.
The news was greeted with anger by local residents.

senses.def: a pattern of straight lines that cross each other to form squares
examples: The streets of Manhattan are laid out in a grid.
Draw a grid on the paper before you start the chart.

senses.def: a network of power lines that carries electricity across an area
examples: The storm knocked out the power grid for three days.
They live off the grid, using solar panels and well water.

note: "Off the grid" = living without public electricity, or hard to contact.

senses.def: deep sadness, especially because someone has died
examples: She was overcome with grief after her husband's death.
Grief counselors were sent to the school after the accident.

senses.def: (informal) trouble or annoyance caused by someone
examples: My boss gave me a lot of grief for being late.

note: "Good grief!" expresses surprise or annoyance. Verb: grieve (for somebody).

senses.def: to smile widely, showing your teeth
examples: He grinned at me from across the room.
She was grinning from ear to ear after the exam.

senses.def: a wide smile
examples: He had a big grin on his face when he heard the news.

note: "Grin and bear it" = accept something unpleasant without complaining.

senses.def: to crush something into very small pieces or powder
examples: I grind fresh coffee beans every morning.
The meat was ground and made into burgers.

senses.def: to rub hard surfaces together, or to make something sharp or smooth by rubbing
examples: He grinds his teeth in his sleep.

senses.def: hard, boring work that continues for a long time
examples: After vacation, it's back to the daily grind.

note: Irregular: grind – ground – ground. "Grind to a halt" = slowly stop completely.

senses.def: a tight hold on something, or control or power over something
examples: Keep a firm grip on the handrail.
The country is in the grip of a severe drought.

senses.def: to hold something very tightly
examples: She gripped the steering wheel nervously.
The child gripped his mother's hand in the crowd.

senses.def: to strongly affect someone or hold their attention
examples: Fear gripped the town after the attacks.
The novel gripped me from the first page.

note: "Get a grip!" (informal) = calm down and control your emotions. "Gripping" = very exciting (a gripping story).

senses.def: a store that sells food and household items (often "grocery store")
examples: I'm stopping at the grocery store on my way home.
The neighborhood grocery closes at nine.

senses.def: (plural) food and other things you buy at a grocery store
examples: Can you help me carry the groceries inside?
We spend about $150 a week on groceries.

note: In American English "grocery store" usually means any supermarket.

senses.def: total, before taxes or costs are taken away
examples: Her gross salary is $80,000, but she takes home much less.
The country's gross domestic product grew by two percent.

senses.def: (informal) very unpleasant or disgusting
examples: Ew, that's gross! There's hair in my soup.

senses.def: very obvious and unacceptable
examples: The hospital was accused of gross negligence.

senses.def: to earn a total amount of money before costs are taken away
examples: The film grossed $300 million worldwide.

note: Opposite of gross (income) is net. "Gross" meaning disgusting is very common in informal American English.

senses.def: the solid surface of the earth, or the soil
examples: She dropped her keys on the ground.
The ground was too hard to dig after the frost.

senses.def: an area of land used for a purpose, or an area of knowledge or discussion
examples: The lecture covered a lot of ground in an hour.
The school sports grounds are open to the public on weekends.

senses.def: (usually plural) a reason for saying or doing something
examples: She was fired on the grounds of misconduct.
There are no grounds for complaint.

senses.def: to stop a plane from flying, or to punish a child by not letting them go out
examples: All flights were grounded because of the storm.
My parents grounded me for a week.

note: "Ground" is also the past form of "grind". "Common ground" = shared opinions or interests.

senses.def: a number of people or things that are together or connected in some way
examples: A group of students was waiting outside the library.
The children worked in small groups.

senses.def: a company that owns several other companies, or a band of musicians
examples: The hotel is owned by a large media group.

senses.def: to put people or things into groups, or to form a group
examples: The books are grouped by subject.
We grouped together under a tree to stay dry.

senses.def: to increase in size, number, or amount, or to become an adult
examples: The town has grown rapidly over the last ten years.
Children grow so fast at this age.

senses.def: to plant and take care of plants, or to let hair get longer
examples: We grow our own vegetables in the backyard.
He's growing a beard for the winter.

senses.def: to gradually become something
examples: The sky grew dark as the storm approached.
She's growing tired of his excuses.

note: Irregular: grow – grew – grown. "Grow up" = become an adult; "grow" alone is used for size and plants.

senses.def: the process of getting bigger or developing physically or mentally
examples: A healthy diet is important for a child's growth.
Travel can be a great opportunity for personal growth.

senses.def: an increase in amount, size, or economic activity
examples: The economy saw strong growth last quarter.
There has been rapid growth in online shopping.

senses.def: a lump of cells that grows abnormally in or on the body
examples: The doctor found a small growth on his skin.

senses.def: a firm promise that something will happen or be done
examples: There's no guarantee that the plan will work.
The laptop comes with a two-year guarantee.

senses.def: to promise that something will happen or that something is true
examples: We guarantee delivery within 24 hours.
Hard work doesn't guarantee success.

note: For products, American English often uses "warranty". Stress is on the last syllable: guar-an-TEE.
